description: Save what this task has established. Each collection is independent: an item that fails does not discard the others, and each one is reported separately. Omission preserves what is already saved. Saving does not finish the task. Collections are optional arrays. Each write must carry at least one item in a nonempty collection or a non-null scalar value; controls alone save nothing. Declare necessary linked changes in groups. Clear, withdraw and added evidence are explicit. A rejected item blocks COMPLETE delivery: resend it under its collection; an accepted version of the same item supersedes the rejected proposal, not a proof that its old scientific claim was corrected. Use a different item identity for an additional fact. Choose disposition PARTIAL to stop with unresolved writes; the host records them in the delivery without marking them repaired.

changes.description:
One fact's sparse change. Name the fact in fact_id and write only the properties
    being changed. A read returns a complete fact, not a write template: omit unchanged
    properties, including empty ones. clear lists optional properties to remove;
    withdraw: true with rationale withdraws the whole fact, keeping history. Repair
    incoming relations in the same group. Use add_source_ids to add evidence while
    retaining earlier evidence. A material is independently addressable. Identity: fact_id. An item sent for a fact_id already saved changes only what it supplies. No other id is needed. kind: COMPOUND, REACTION, OPERATION, MATERIAL, CONDITION, OUTCOME, TARGET, NOTE. status: ACCEPTED, CONTEXT, REJECTED, UNRESOLVED. extent: WHOLE_OWNERS, WITHIN_OWNER.

after.description: Operation predecessors within its reaction. Preserve or explicitly rebuild order when replacing operations.

category.description: The kind's role: for an OPERATION or NOTE use the task's native fact meanings. For a CONDITION: Prefer one of these keys, written as such: TEMPERATURE: a temperature the reaction is held at or brought to (reflux, -78 °C, rt); several on one operation are its profile in the order written; DURATION: how long the operation or a stage of it runs (2 h, overnight); ATMOSPHERE: the gas the reaction is run under (argon, N2, air, H2 balloon); PRESSURE: the pressure the reaction is run at (4 atm H2, 50 bar); the vacuum of a concentration or distillation is REDUCED_PRESSURE, not this; CONCENTRATION: the concentration of the reaction mixture (0.1 M, c = 0.05 M); the strength of a reagent's solution (2.5 M in hexanes, 1 M in THF) is part of that material's amount phrase, not a condition of its own; SCALE: the amount the operation is run on; on a MATERIAL, how much of it the author used: his whole phrase for the amount, copied as written with every quantity and qualifier in it (26 mg (0.25 mmol, 1 equiv), 1.1 mL (0.55 mmol, 0.5 M in THF), 10 mol %, ten drops); the host reads the amount and the equivalents from it; ADDITION: how or in what order a material is added (dropwise, portionwise, over 30 min, added last); WORKUP: how the reaction is quenched, washed or extracted; purification does not by itself create a separate operation. Its media are QUENCH_WORKUP materials; MICROWAVE: heated by microwave irradiation (MW, μW); PHOTOCHEMICAL: driven by light: a lamp, LED or hv at a wavelength; keeping light out is LIGHT_EXCLUSION; SONICATION: run under ultrasound (sonication, ultrasonic bath); FLOW: run in continuous flow or a flow reactor rather than a flask; SEALED_VESSEL: run in a sealed tube, pressure tube, autoclave or bomb; an ordinary flask is not a condition; DEGASSED: the mixture or solvent was degassed (freeze-pump-thaw, sparged with an inert gas); bubbling a reactive gas through is that gas's ATMOSPHERE; ONE_POT: carried out in the same pot as the preceding operation without isolation (one-pot, telescoped, tandem); STOCK_SOLUTION: how a reagent solution was supplied or handled for use (titrated before use); the strength of a reagent's solution (2.5 M in hexanes, 1 M in THF) is part of that material's amount phrase, not a condition of its own. A separately prepared reagent is one material of the main operation. Its preparation ingredients and preparation conditions belong to another experiment: retain that procedure with its source and explanation, without adding its ingredients or conditions to the main operation. In an experimental reading, ANOTHER_EXPERIMENT keeps the reading separate. Preserve the complete account through the declared narrative entry; if the active declaration offers EXPERIMENT and its operations through skeleton_repairs, use those for an independent experimental graph. A narrative alone does not create that graph.; MONITORING: how completion was judged (monitored by TLC, until consumption of the starting material); STIRRING: a stated stirring or agitation regime (vigorous stirring, rpm); REDUCED_PRESSURE: under vacuum for a concentration, distillation or removal of a volatile (in vacuo, rotary evaporation, reduced pressure); LIGHT_EXCLUSION: kept from light (amber flask, wrapped in foil, in the dark); SOLVENT_RATIO: the proportion of mixed reaction solvents (THF:H2O 4:1, 8:1 THF/1 M NaOH); the solvents themselves are MATERIALs. Chromatography eluents and their ratios belong to QUENCH_WORKUP materials. If none fits, write your own word here and the host keeps the condition with a null key; text is always the author's own words. For a MATERIAL: Choose one of these roles by its meaning: ROUTE_SUBSTRATE: the route compound the operation starts from and transforms, however the author names or numbers it; REAGENT: a substance added to bring the transformation about and consumed by it (a base, an oxidant, a reductant, an organometallic, an acid); CATALYST: a substance that brings the transformation about without being consumed by it (a metal complex, an organocatalyst, an acid or base used catalytically); ADDITIVE: a substance added to the reaction that is neither its reagent, its catalyst nor its solvent (a ligand, a salt, molecular sieves, an initiator, a stabilizer); SOLVENT: the medium the reaction itself runs in; a solvent used only to quench, extract, wash or purify is QUENCH_WORKUP; QUENCH_WORKUP: anything used after the reaction to stop it or to isolate or purify its product: a quench, a wash, an extraction solvent, a drying agent, a chromatography eluent (its ratio kept in its name), silica or celite. For an OUTCOME: Choose one of these kinds by its meaning: ISOLATED_YIELD: the yield of a product the author isolated, with or without its mass (2.65 g (97%), 42 mg (52%), 70% isolated yield); REPORTED_YIELD: a yield the author states without saying how it was determined, as a scheme or the narrative often does (81% over 3 steps, quantitative); ASSAY_YIELD: a yield measured on the unpurified mixture by GC, HPLC or another calibrated assay; NMR_YIELD: a yield measured on the unpurified mixture by NMR against an internal standard; BRSM_YIELD: a yield based on recovered starting material (71% brsm); EE: the product's enantiomeric excess (98% ee); DR: the product's diastereomeric ratio, a single diastereomer included (3:1 dr, >20:1 d.r., single diastereomer); RATIO: any other ratio between products or isomers (E/Z 5:1, a regioisomer ratio, an enantiomeric ratio); RECOVERED_STARTING_MATERIAL: how much starting material was recovered unreacted (15% rsm, 323 mg (37%) of the starting diastereomer); SCALE: how much product a run made where the author states an amount but no yield (1.52 g of 14b); the amount a run is carried out on is the SCALE condition, not this.

clear.description: Explicitly clear optional properties of an existing fact. On a new fact an empty value is simply its default; on an existing fact omission preserves the property and clearing it is said here, never by sending an empty value. Required scientific content and relations cannot be emptied.

extent.description: Condition or measurement scope: whole owners or a substage explained in rationale.

fact_id.description: The fact this change is about: an existing fact by its id as the progress lists it (a read location here instead binds the version you read); a fact created in this write by a name of your choosing, given here and nowhere else. The host binds identity and compares with the version a write naming no view is compared with (view says which).

inputs.description: For a REACTION, the compound facts it consumes: its block boundary.

kind.description: The fact's kind; required for a new fact, omitted for an existing one. Use the native fact meanings in the task instructions.

labels.description: Author-assigned labels only, not names or explanations. For one mixture, give all component labels (9a and 9b); its identity uses the complete label set, not its first member. A single component and the mixture are different identities.

outputs.description: For a REACTION, the compound facts it forms; for an OUTCOME, the products it identifies.

owners.description: Exact subjects: operation belongs to reaction; material to operation; condition to operation OR material; outcome to operations.

rationale.description: Explain the source meaning behind a correction, context role or identity; do not fill missing evidence by inference.

same_as.description: Explicit source-supported identity with another fact. Labels alone do not establish identity. Use clear to remove the relation.

source_ids.description: Keys in the supplied immutable source index supporting the change, never invented citations.

status.description: The fact's evidential status; assign it only to change it.

text.description: Scientific content. For COMPOUND, only its source-supported name or designation; put author labels in labels and explanations in rationale or a sourced NOTE. Names do not establish structure or cross-figure identity. For a MATERIAL: One material name selected from the cited wording. Keep chemically meaningful isotopes, charges and subscripts; a trailing reference marker need not be copied. The host locates the chosen words in the unchanged source; matching is not a chemical identity judgment. For an OUTCOME: The author's words for one reported value, copied as written with the mass and basis written with it ("1.58 g (57% over 2 steps)", "84% brsm", "dr = 3:1"). Two values written together are two phrases: "71% (84% brsm)" is "71%" and "84% brsm". The host reads the number and the basis from these words; do not calculate or restate them. Omission preserves. To remove an optional statement, name it in clear.

withdraw.description: Withdraw this fact with a rationale, keeping history. Fix necessary incoming relations in the same group; no cascade deletion.

experiment_assessments.description: Whether the MAIN experimental investigation of these subjects is sufficient. Identity: subject_ids, in any order. An item sent again with the same subject_ids replaces the saved one. No other id is needed. status: SUFFICIENT, NEEDS_READ, UNRESOLVED.

explanation.description: The reasoning, and the assessment's only prose field: a rationale or a limitation goes here.

source_ids.description: Keys in the supplied source index supporting the assessment.

status.description: SUFFICIENT only when the MAIN experimental investigation actually is; NEEDS_READ with the remaining direction; UNRESOLVED with its limitation.

subject_ids.description: The exact facts or navigation segments assessed.

groups.description:
Changes that stand or fall together: changes written inline, or fact_ids naming items
    sent under changes in this same write, with a reason. Unrelated items stay independent.

fact_ids.description: Instead of inline changes: the fact_id of items sent under changes in this same write that belong to this group. The host moves them into the group.

reason.description: Why these changes belong together; may be left empty.

note.description: Scientific integration: source meaning, decisions and remaining limitations.

overview.description: The whole route in a few sentences. Set it or leave it.

questions.description: One scoped question and its status; only new or changed questions are written. Identity: question_id (your own name for it). An item sent again with the same question_id replaces the saved one. No other id is needed. status: RESOLVED, UNRESOLVED, WAIT_FOR_SI, CAPABILITY_LIMIT.

explanation.description: Why this status, grounded in the evidence read or the resolution reached.

question.description: A neutral, self-contained question stating the investigation range, the remaining issue and the expected output.

status.description: Scientific question status. RESOLVED: Stop this question with the actual result or evidenced conclusion supplied. UNRESOLVED: Stop this question for now with a stated limitation. WAIT_FOR_SI: Stop MAIN investigation with an explicit SI dependency; does not assert SI exists. CAPABILITY_LIMIT: Stop because the required interpretation cannot be expressed or performed.

subject_ids.description: The facts or navigation segments this question is about.

text_block_ids.description: Authorized MAIN text blocks from the catalog this concerns.

visual_ids.description: Authorized MAIN images from the catalog this concerns.

repairs.description: Optional. An accepted new version of the same item supersedes its rejected proposal; this does not prove the old scientific claim was saved. To declare a correction/replacement explicitly, give the rejected row's action_id and the corrected item's key in this write, spelled as receipts spell item: collection:index for a listed item, or the envelope's own name.

items.description: Two keys copied from receipts: the rejected row's action_id, the corrected item's item.

action_id.description: Copy the action_id of the rejected row from the receipt that listed it. The host assigns action_ids to receipt rows; items carry none.

item.description: The corrected item's key in this write, spelled as receipts spell item: collection:index for a listed item, or the envelope's own name.

segments.description: Navigation scope linking observations to work; never a second executable graph. Identity: segment_id (your own name for it). An item sent again with the same segment_id replaces the saved one. No other id is needed.

scope.description: The part of the route this segment covers, in words; a step range or a rationale goes here, and a segment has no other prose field.

source_ids.description: Keys in the supplied source index locating this scope, never invented.

view.description: Optional. The version of this result the write was revised from, when it is older than the one the host would otherwise compare with: the view_location a read of 'current' returned. Without view, or with 'current', that version is the later of the latest progress and what your own last write left.
